meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 6 (Multi-Select): Client Best Practices
meta.format: multi_select: questions use the 'answers' array (multiple correct options). Some include an 'All of the above' option that is only correct when every other option is.

questions.question: Which implementation guidelines apply to progressive tool discovery? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Offer multiple detail levels (name-only, name+description, full schema)
Cache tool definitions host-side once fetched
Refresh the search catalog when notifications/tools/list_changed arrives
Group tools by their source server
Re-sort the tools array on every turn to keep it alphabetical

questions.explanation: The first four are the documented guidelines. Re-sorting the tools array mid-conversation is an anti-pattern — it invalidates provider prompt caches.

questions.question: Which security considerations apply to programmatic tool calling (code mode)? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Per-call authorization: approving the script does not grant blanket approval for every runtime call
The sandbox should have no direct network access
API keys and tokens stay with the host broker, never exposed to generated code
Tool results from one server can be trusted as clean input to another server
Set timeouts and memory limits, and validate/truncate sandbox output before returning it to the model

questions.explanation: All listed protections are documented except D: cross-server data flow is explicitly untrusted — tool results from one server are untrusted input to another, and the broker applies the same review policy as for direct calls.

questions.question: Which discovery strategies does the guide list for implementing a search_tools meta-tool? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Keyword-based matching (BM25, regex)
Embedding-based vector similarity
Subagent-based selection using a small fast model
Hybrid combinations of the above
Round-robin rotation through all tools

questions.explanation: Keyword, embedding, subagent, and hybrid are the four strategies; providers' built-in tool search may be preferred when available. Round-robin isn't a strategy.

questions.question: To preserve provider prompt caching while doing progressive discovery, which practices does the guide recommend? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Append newly discovered definitions after the cache breakpoint instead of re-sorting the tools array
Route every call through a single stable call_tool({name, args}) meta-tool so the array never changes
Treat server disconnection as a conversation-boundary operation rather than per-turn
Remove and re-add tool definitions each turn to keep context minimal
Consult the provider's caching documentation

questions.explanation: Adding/removing definitions mid-conversation invalidates the cached prompt prefix and can cost more than it saves — exactly what option D would cause.

questions.question: When does the client-best-practices guide say progressive tool discovery pays off? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: When connected servers expose large tool catalogs that would consume a noticeable share of the context window (roughly the 1–5%+ territory)
When tool definitions crowd out room for actual conversation
When most tools are irrelevant to any single task
When the host connects to exactly one server exposing two tools
All of the above

questions.explanation: Progressive discovery trades latency for context savings — worthwhile for large catalogs, pointless overhead for two tools.

questions.question: In the code-mode architecture, which security properties does the guide require or recommend? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The sandbox has no direct network access — all tool calls go through the host broker
Credentials live with the broker and are never injected into generated code
Each runtime tool call is authorized individually; approving the script is not blanket approval
isError tool results surface as exceptions the generated code can handle
All of the above

questions.explanation: All four are the documented pillars of safe programmatic tool calling, so E is genuinely correct.

questions.question: Which practices protect provider prompt caches during a long agentic session? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Keeping the tools array byte-stable and appending new definitions only after the cache breakpoint
Relying on servers returning tools/list in deterministic order
Routing execution through one stable call_tool meta-tool so definitions never churn
Re-shuffling tool order each turn to surface the most relevant tools first
All of the above

questions.explanation: Re-ordering is the classic cache-killer — the spec even added the deterministic-order recommendation (minor change 3) for exactly this reason.

questions.question: Which steps make up the progressive-discovery loop? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Catalog: fetch lightweight tool identities (names, short descriptions)
Inspect: pull the full schema only for candidate tools
Execute: call the chosen tool with validated arguments
Retrain: fine-tune the model on the tool schemas
All of the above

questions.explanation: Catalog → inspect → execute is the loop; no fine-tuning is involved anywhere in MCP.
